title: Best Healthcare & Medical Privacy Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare top healthcare privacy tools for protecting medical data, health apps, and telehealth. HIPAA compliance, encryption, and security features analyzed.
intro: Your medical data is incredibly valuable to data brokers and advertisers. From health apps selling your information to unsecured telehealth platforms, protecting your healthcare privacy requires the right tools and knowledge of HIPAA gaps.

verdict.summary: For comprehensive healthcare privacy, use Incognito Browser for secure web browsing and telehealth, Signal for encrypted messaging with healthcare providers, and ExpressVPN for additional connection security. ProtonMail adds encrypted email capabilities for formal healthcare correspondence.

pro_tips: Always use Incognito Browser when researching health conditions online to prevent building a medical profile that could affect insurance or employment.
Set up Signal with healthcare providers who are willing to use encrypted messaging - many progressive practices now offer this option.
Use a VPN like ExpressVPN when accessing telehealth platforms from public WiFi or unsecured networks to protect your medical consultations.
Create separate email accounts with ProtonMail specifically for healthcare communications to compartmentalize your medical privacy.
Regularly audit your health apps' privacy settings and delete those that share data with third parties - most period trackers and fitness apps sell your information.

faqs.question: Are health apps covered by HIPAA?
faqs.answer: Most health apps are NOT covered by HIPAA. Only apps used directly by HIPAA-covered entities (like hospitals) are protected. Consumer health apps, fitness trackers, and period trackers can legally sell your data to advertisers and data brokers.

faqs.question: Can I use these tools for telehealth appointments?
faqs.answer: Yes, but check with your healthcare provider first. While tools like Signal offer better security than standard platforms, many providers are required to use specific HIPAA-compliant telehealth platforms. You can still use Incognito Browser and a VPN to access their chosen platform securely.

faqs.question: How do I protect my period tracking data?
faqs.answer: Avoid apps that share data with third parties. Use privacy-focused options or track offline. If using any period tracking app, always use Incognito Browser to prevent cross-site tracking and consider a VPN to hide your location data from the app provider.

faqs.question: What medical information do data brokers collect?
faqs.answer: Data brokers collect prescription purchases, health app data, fitness tracker information, search history for medical conditions, and location data from medical facilities. They create detailed health profiles sold to insurers, employers, and marketers.

faqs.question: Is encrypted email necessary for healthcare communications?
faqs.answer: While not legally required for patient communications, encrypted email protects sensitive health information from being intercepted, stored by email providers, or accessed by hackers. It's especially important for reproductive health information and mental health communications.
